direct_answer: Polarity inversion flips the entire waveform vertically; phase describes a frequency-dependent time relationship between signals. A polarity flip can improve one blend but is not a universal phase-alignment command. For this concept question, the useful next step is not to chase a meter or preset: run one controlled comparison and decide from the musical consequence.

steps: Save a Project Alternative or record the current channel, routing, pan mode, polarity, delay, width, and automation state.
Blend the two related signals at matched level, toggle polarity on one, then compare both settings in stereo and mono without moving any timing.
Compare the same musical passage at matched loudness in full context, then repeat the important part in mono.

title: Phase Versus Polarity — what it changes
tradeoffs: A polarity flip can improve one frequency region while worsening another when the real issue is arrival-time difference.
A change that increases apparent width or loudness may be preferred before mono translation and center stability are judged.
A local improvement can create a new balance, localization, depth, or arrangement problem.
